description: Differences between a Java-built HPDS phenotype store and a Rust-built one that the spec (brain/rust-hpds-phenotype/spec.md) accepts. etl-parity-compare.py whitelists a difference when its kind is in a rule's kinds, the case's loader is in the rule's loaders (when given), and the rule's condition holds. Every other difference is unexpected and fails the run.

ignoredColumnMetaColumns.name: block-offset
ignoredColumnMetaColumns.spec: Deliberate divergences: columnMeta.csv columns 8 and 9 hold the block offset and length. Java writes the javabin offset and end position.
ignoredColumnMetaColumns.reason: Java writes the javabin offset; Rust writes the offset in pheno.blocks. The dictionary ETL stores the column as an unused string.

ignoredColumnMetaColumns.name: block-length
ignoredColumnMetaColumns.spec: Deliberate divergences: columnMeta.csv columns 8 and 9 hold the block offset and length. Java writes the javabin offset and end position.
ignoredColumnMetaColumns.reason: Java writes the javabin end position; Rust writes the block length in pheno.blocks.

rules.name: loading-cache-overwrite
rules.spec: Deliberate divergences: Both Java loaders keep one (LowRAM) or 16 (new-search) concepts in a loading cache and overwrite a concept's metadata when its rows are not contiguous in ingest order, losing the earlier rows.
rules.reason: The Java loader evicted the concept from its loading cache, created a fresh cube when the concept came back, and kept only the last cube's rows and metadata. Every Java row is also in the Rust store; Rust keeps every row.

rules.name: lowram-lost-last-chunk
rules.spec: Deliberate divergences: LowRAM also loses its last chunk when the file has more lines than records, and rows of a concept split across 5 GiB chunks. Rust keeps every row.
rules.reason: LowRAMCSVProcessor counts physical lines, so a quoted field holding a line break leaves the last chunk unflushed and its records are never ingested. Every Java row is also in the Rust store.

rules.name: lowram-lost-last-chunk-patients
rules.spec: Deliberate divergences: LowRAM also loses its last chunk when the file has more lines than records. Rust keeps every row.
rules.reason: The patient only has rows in the chunk LowRAM never ingested, so it never reached allIds.

rules.name: lowram-max-double-min-value
rules.spec: Deliberate divergences: LowRAMLoadingStore.complete and LoadingStore (CSVLoaderNewSearch) initialize max to Double.MIN_VALUE (the smallest positive double), so a concept with only negative values reports a max of 4.9E-324. Rust reports the real max.
rules.reason: Java starts max at Double.MIN_VALUE, so a numeric concept whose real max is zero or negative reports 4.9E-324.

rules.name: empty-numeric-concept-min-max
rules.spec: Deliberate divergences: An empty numeric concept gets null min and max in Rust. Java writes 1.7976931348623157E308 and 4.9E-324.
rules.reason: Every row of the numeric concept was dropped. Java prints its initial min and max; Rust prints null.

rules.name: newsearch-crashes-on-unparseable-value
rules.spec: Deliberate divergences: CSVLoaderNewSearch crashes on an unparseable number or timestamp, and LowRAM crashes on a one-field row or invalid UTF-8. Rust drops and counts the row or timestamp, and decodes UTF-8 lossily.
rules.reason: CSVLoaderNewSearch calls Double.parseDouble and Long.parseLong without a catch, so the Java load stops with a NumberFormatException and writes no store.

rules.name: lowram-crashes-on-one-field-row-or-bad-utf8
rules.spec: Deliberate divergences: LowRAM crashes on a one-field row or invalid UTF-8. Rust drops and counts the row, and decodes UTF-8 lossily.
rules.reason: LowRAMCSVProcessor sorts each chunk on field 1 before checking the field count, and counts lines with Files.lines, which rejects invalid UTF-8.

params.pattern: (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException: Index 1 out of bounds for length 1|MalformedInputException)

rules.name: negative-patient-ids-rejected
rules.spec: Parity rules: Negative patient IDs: Java int allows them, roaring is u32. The ETL rejects them with a clear error until we know whether any real dataset has them. Decisions 6: the ETL and migrate reject them with an error naming the first offending row.
rules.reason: hpds-etl refuses a negative patient number; the Java outcome is recorded in the case report.

params.pattern: PATIENT_NUM is not an integer between 0 and 2147483647

rules.name: long-min-timestamp-is-no-timestamp
rules.spec: Timestamps: Java has two no-timestamp values, null and Long.MIN_VALUE (from the two-argument KeyAndValue constructor). Both map to i64::MIN.
rules.reason: DumpSourceCSV prints a Long.MIN_VALUE timestamp as -9223372036854775808; the Rust store cannot tell it from no timestamp and prints an empty field.

rules.name: double-to-string-format
rules.spec: Parity rules: Double.toString vs Rust {} formatting differ in the canonical dump (1.0E10 vs 10000000000). The dump compares parsed values, not strings.
rules.reason: The two sides print the same double differently.
